title: Duo App Index
scope: Independent documentation audit; not a device-tested compatibility certification.
methodology: Each record is keyed by its numeric App Store ID, not app name. Only the US storefront is used for the app record.
Discovery used Apple editorial collections, Apple Newsroom, multiple independent directories and focused searches. Third-party labels were treated as leads, not confirmation.
The app description, own in-app event metadata and visible App Store version history were inspected. Reviews and recommended-app metadata were excluded.

An explicit iPhone Duo reference in released notes, an affirmative developer description/event, or Apple optimized-app curation qualifies as documented support. This establishes a published claim, not defect-free behavior.
Generic iOS updates, a recent build date, iPad support and popularity on Duo do not independently prove Duo optimization.

Earliest visible support note is the oldest qualifying entry exposed in the inspected history. It may be later than the real first supporting version. Repeated historical release notes can complicate dating.
Future-only announcements are excluded from shipped release evidence. Announced apps remain separate until rollout is established.
Detailed feature notes are individually curated for a shortlist. Other records establish support documentation only; they do not assert particular layouts.
No hands-on device tests were performed. Full-screen, crease avoidance, tabletop behavior, Split View and external-display preview remain untested unless a future test record says otherwise.
An app absent from the documented list may still work well. No claim of exhaustive App Store coverage is made.
Video aspect-ratio bars are not the same as an app being letterboxed. A support badge is not a guarantee that every screen or feature is optimized.

changelog.change: Initial audit of 661 app records; 605 have qualifying support documentation. Release-note evidence, description evidence and Apple curation are labeled separately.
